In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the performance of the IEEE 802. 11p physical layer depends on the antenna height of the RSUs and that the performance can be significantly improved if the antenna height is increased.
the required SNR is dependent on the antenna height and the packet length.
the required SNR is not only dependent on the antenna height, but also on the packet length and the data rate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a RSU with the antenna mounted higher is more suitable for the application of cooperative driving.
for infrastructure-to-vehicle communication the required SNR can be reduced by mounting the antenna higher and by increasing the packet length.
for the high RSUs a FER less than 0,1 can be achieved with a required SNR of about 10 dB, while for the low RSUs about 14 dB is needed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the required SNR is highly dependent on the RSU antenna height and packet length.
for a realistic RSU deployment the physical layer performance depends significantly on the RSU antenna height.
a low mounted RSU antenna is not suitable for infrastructure-to-vehicle communication in a realistic environment.
